baseline.method: Full documents.json.gz text inventory without slot-tag filtering; actual installed BodyReader.record and photo_canonical_source.native inspected for six nearby CIDs; native content matched current V3 content for all six. V3 raw JSON was not equated to V4 raw JSON.
baseline.scope_limit: Token inventory is a locator aid, not semantic absence proof. The six source-body reviews and top8 meaning inspection support this limited object-family diagnosis.

confusion_boundaries: Subject identifies the visible entity the photograph is about; still-life/product/editorial are genres or presentation contexts.
Color belongs to a declared existing carrier; selective red color cannot identify a teapot or justify changing other objects.
An accessory such as a violin bow remains a separate owner and does not establish the whole instrument.
Integral object parts identify the same owner; a lid, attached handle and spout do not independently add teapots. Subject naming does not authorize a group count.
This set adds particular recognizable design options. It does not impose these parts on every object sharing the category, or change the existing subject count.

Museum attribution, age, origin, function and material require appropriate declaration/evidence; visual resemblance alone does not establish authenticity or working condition. Ceramic and wooden-body declarations are explicit candidate material effects.
Primary-entity identification supplies neither a fixed crop nor composition, lighting, background, color, operator, active use, props or steam. These remain separately governed.
recommendations: Integrate these four distinct complete object subjects with source notes and narrow owner properties; keep all discovery-only pending independent native review.
Keep original probe bytes fixed during before/after search. Review whether a concrete type is exposed separately from its native eligibility and red-color compatibility.
Use the three independent additional intents to check coverage beyond the known teapot probe; do not alter generic style records or boost slot tags.
Treat an object-type match as semantic subject evidence only. A candidate that also declares material must retain that material effect during adoption review.
